svg.title: dbt Lineage: Staging Views to the wh_gold Star Schema
svg.desc: A flow diagram tracing dbt model lineage. Two staging views, stg_positions and stg_returns, read silver Delta sources in the lakehouse. Three dimension models — dim_date, dim_portfolio, dim_benchmark — and one SCD Type 2 dimension, dim_instrument, build from those staging views. Four incremental fact models — fact_positions, fact_returns_daily, fact_risk_measures, fact_transactions — join the staging views to the dimensions. All four facts converge on the wh_gold star schema, which Direct Lake serves to Power BI. A warning node calls out the one dimension using SCD Type 2 history against three that overwrite in place, and the adapter limitation that makes dbt's incremental MERGE work on Fabric Warehouse at all.
svg.text: wh_gold star schema — The published gold layer: four facts joined to conformed dimensions in the warehouse.Gold Star Schema & dbt Lineage — wh_gold (Fabric Warehouse)
silver (lh_analytics) → dbt staging views → dims + facts, built by dbt-fabric
DBT STAGING VIEWS (1:1 with silver, light cleanup)
source() reads silver via 3-part cross-database name

text.aria-label: SCD Type 2 only on one dimension

svg.text: SCD Type 2 only on one dimension — Mixing one Type 2 dimension with three Type 1 dimensions in the same gold layer is a real design tension to manage deliberately.DIMENSIONS (wh_gold)
dim_instrument (SCD Type 2) — The one dimension in gold that preserves full attribute history via SCD Type 2.dim_instrument
dim_date — A conventional calendar dimension joined by every fact model.✓ relationships → dim_date,
dim_portfolio — A conformed portfolio dimension built from stg_positions, joined by every fact.dim_instrument, dim_portfolio
fact_returns_daily (incremental) — Daily time-weighted returns by portfolio, joined to benchmark and date.daily portfolio & benchmark returns
dim_benchmark — A conformed benchmark dimension built from stg_returns, joined by return and risk facts.dim_portfolio, dim_benchmark
fact_risk_measures (incremental) — VaR, exposures, and sensitivities by portfolio and instrument, joined via the effective-dated instrument key.VaR, exposures, sensitivities
avoid full-table CTAS rebuild on large facts
not_null on every FK · unique on natural keys where applicable
fact_transactions (incremental) — Buys, sells, corporate actions, and cash flows, keyed by source system and transaction id.(fact_transactions.transaction_id) · relationships tests enforce
every FK resolves to a valid dim row — dbt build fails the run if not
dbt-fabric adapter (community-maintained, pip install dbt-fabric) compiles every model to T-SQL and runs it as CREATE TABLE AS SELECT (CTAS) plus DROP/CREATE —
Fabric Warehouse's T-SQL surface does not support full ALTER semantics, so dbt materializes tables rather than altering them in place, except where "incremental" models merge new rows.
An Apache Airflow job inside Data Factory triggers `dbt build` (run + test) on a schedule, so every gold rebuild is immediately validated by the unique/not_null/relationships tests shown above.

stg_positions (staging view) — A dbt staging view reading silver positions from the lakehouse via a three-part source name.Silver = source tables in lh_analytics, read by dbt's source() via three-part cross-database name (lakehouse.schema.table)

stg_returns (staging view) — A dbt staging view reading silver daily returns from the lakehouse.Staging views (stg_*) = 1:1 light-cleanup views over silver, the only models allowed to reference source() directly
Dimensions (dim_*) = conformed reference tables shared by every fact, rebuilt via CTAS on each dbt run
Facts (fact_*) = measure tables at a stated grain, joined to dims by surrogate keys
= schema.yml test annotation shown on the model — unique, not_null, or relationships (fails the dbt build if violated)

fact_positions (incremental) — Daily position holdings by portfolio and instrument, built incrementally.= incremental materialization mark (fact_transactions, fact_returns_daily) — merges new rows instead of full CTAS rebuild
= foreign-key join between a fact and a dimension (enforced by a relationships test)
